I had been taking my dog to Dr. Peter Gusmorino  whom I did like for about a year and a half without any issues. When his previous office closed, I wanted to continue seeing the same veterinarian, so I followed him to this location.

On November 14, 2023, I had a 1:15 PM appointment. This was my first visit to this clinic. 1:15 came and went, and after waiting for hours, around 3:30 PM a man yelled at my dog and told him to “shut up.” I responded, and an argument followed. Eventually, the man left the office, and I believed the situation was over.

Shortly afterward, a staff member approached me in an accusatory manner and poked me. I began recording because I felt uncomfortable and wanted to document what was happening. At no point did I touch anyone, threaten anyone, or call anyone names.

When I pointed out that multiple people in the waiting room had witnessed what happened, I felt that my concerns were dismissed rather than addressed. Another staff member repeatedly said, “Just kick her out,” while holding the door. I was told that if I continued recording, my dog would not be seen. Although I agreed to sit down and wait, staff later called the police instead of resolving the situation professionally.

What upset me most was that I felt singled out and unfairly treated throughout the interaction. I have video recordings of portions of the incident, including a witness who told me he saw the entire situation and did not believe I was at fault.

As someone who lives with PTSD, this experience was extremely upsetting. I expected professionalism, respect, and concern for both clients and their pets. Instead, I left feeling humiliated and unwelcome.

Based on my experience, I will be filing a formal complaint and sharing my concerns with the appropriate authorities. Pet owners deserve to feel safe, respected, and confident in the care their animals receive.

They care for our fur babies the same way we do and understand that as pet parents, some decisions are difficult to make, and they hold space for that. It’s wonderful to have a neighborhood community come together in this clinic, and I’m thankful that they are still present in our neighborhood. Thank you for being here. May you continue to grow and be even more abundant as time moves on. Thank you 🙏🏽

First of all, the front desk reception is as awful as all the other reviews say. And for emergency pet care, costumer service REALLY makes a difference. This is a clear problem that has been brought up by several costumers that is not being properly addressed. Second, Animal Hospital of Brooklyn changed from working with secondary pharmacies like Chewy, to only working with their pharmacy. We were not told of this transition (although AHOB insistent that they had sent us an email stating this transition, which they hadn’t), and as a result we ran out of critical medication for our cat, which resulted in her needing to be hospitalized. I would also like to note that our medication from their pharmacy not only costs 15$ more than it does from other pharmacies, but the delivery time is also twice as long. It is also unpredictable, I will order her medication with an estimated shipping of 1 week and then it will end up being 2 or even 3 weeks before the medication actually arrives. I can’t for the life of me understand why this transition was made if not for a cash grab. Third and finally, my cat was hospitalized for severe constipation and given a procedure of deobstipation without even so much as discussing it with me first. Later on, she was hospitalized at another vet and needed the same procedure but the doctor made sure to go over all the risks associated with me before they began the procedure, as it can be risky and invasive. AHOB gave her 4 enemas before completing this procedure, but the other doctor gave her 8 enemas, insisting that deobstipation should be a last resort (might I note that the deobstipation procedure is incredibly expensive, in comparison to enemas which can be more cost efficient). On another occasion, we had brought her in around 2 hours before close to get one enema and we were told that they didn’t have time that day to perform the enema so she would need to stay over (costing us a large hospitalization fee). But at our other doctor, we did the same thing and they performed the enema and discharged her within 30 minutes. I have given this hospital the benefit of the doubt over and over again but they have demonstrated time after time a priority of finances over the wellbeing of their animals. I highly do not recommend Animal Hospital of Brooklyn.
